# AI- og tech-aktier flyver videre - men hvor længe?

**Feed**: millionaerklubben  
**Published**: 2026-08-27  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Danish Millionærklubben episode centres on Nvidia's strong earnings: revenue roughly doubled, and management signalled about 70% revenue growth next fiscal year, capped by supply limits. The panel also covers AI adoption turning AI into a 'workforce', a possible turnaround at Salesforce helped by its Anthropic partnership, strong CrowdStrike results with Palo Alto preferred on valuation, and Meta's settlement over harm to young users. The overall tone on AI/tech is constructive, though guest Christian Kongsted prefers AMD, Micron, Lam Research and Intel over Nvidia in his portfolio, and the Danish market is flat because it has little tech exposure.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟠 NVDA — Nvidia | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Guest relatively positive, sees valuation 30-50% below sector on cash flows, but doesn't own it; prefers other semis.

#### Reasoning

Guest Christian Kongsted: blowout quarter, ~70% FY growth indication vs ~44% expected, supply-constrained demand, rising GPU rental prices. Two-year-forward multiples look low (~17x P/E) because of priced-in risks (circular investments, competition, in-house chips). If those risks fade, the stock could re-rate. His algorithm ranks other semis higher, so it is not bought now.

#### Sell Triggers

- GPU rental prices turn down
- hyperscalers successfully replace Nvidia chips with in-house silicon
- circular AI investment risks materialise

> *"Jeg er sådan relativt positiv på aktien, må jeg sige."*

---

### 🟢 AMD — AMD | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Held by guest; outperformed Nvidia this year; algorithm favours it within AI semis.

#### Reasoning

Guest positioned in AMD, Lam Research, Micron and Intel instead of Nvidia based on his quantitative algorithm; AMD attacking Nvidia frontally with competitive chips and strong YTD returns.

#### Sell Triggers

- GPU demand/rental prices reverse
- algorithm ranking changes in favour of Nvidia

> *"AMD, som Ben nævner, har for eksempel klaret sig væsentligt bedre i år"*

---

### 🟢 LRCX — Lam Research | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Named among guest's algorithm-selected AI supply-chain holdings.

#### Reasoning

Guest prefers names further down the AI supply chain; Lam Research ranks above Nvidia in his algorithm.

#### Sell Triggers

- AI capex slowdown
- algorithm ranking changes

> *"det er sådan noget som LAM Research, det er Micron, det er AMD, det er Intel"*

---

### 🟢 MU — Micron | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Algorithm-selected holding; memory chip shortages constrain AI hardware supply.

#### Reasoning

Guest's algorithm favours Micron; memory constraints noted as bottleneck limiting Nvidia output, implying pricing power for memory makers.

#### Sell Triggers

- memory shortage eases
- AI capex slowdown

> *"det er sådan noget som LAM Research, det er Micron, det er AMD, det er Intel"*

---

### 🟢 INTC — Intel | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Named among guest's algorithm-favoured semi positions.

#### Reasoning

Only mentioned as part of the guest's algorithm-driven semi basket preferred over Nvidia; no specific thesis given.

#### Sell Triggers

- algorithm ranking changes

> *"det er sådan noget som LAM Research, det er Micron, det er AMD, det er Intel"*

---

### 🟢 PANW — Palo Alto Networks | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Guest holds PANW over CrowdStrike: similar AI-security leadership at roughly half the valuation.

#### Reasoning

Cybersecurity is accelerating as AI powers both attack and defence; PANW and CRWD lead (both previewed Anthropic's Mythos). Guest chooses PANW for more reasonable pricing vs CrowdStrike's ~2x multiples.

#### Sell Triggers

- valuation gap to CrowdStrike closes
- loss of AI security leadership

> *"Så prissætningen er mere rimelig over i Palo Alto Networks"*

---

### 🟠 CRWD — CrowdStrike | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Excellent results (ARR +51%) and 'does everything right', but valuation seen as priced for perfection.

#### Reasoning

Guest calls it a super company with strong upsell on Falcon platform and Falcon Flex +100%, but multiples ~2x Palo Alto's make him prefer PANW. Quality name to watch for better entry.

#### Sell Triggers

- growth deceleration given rich valuation
- execution misstep

> *"CrowdStrike, de er nærmest prissat som om, de skal placere en mand på månen"*

---

### 🟠 CRM — Salesforce | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Signs of turnaround (rev +11%, bookings +14%, Anthropic deal), but guest warns CEO may overinterpret; product execution questioned.

#### Reasoning

Guest positive on Anthropic partnership and early AgentForce traction after a beaten-down year, but notes a slow enterprise sales cycle and was early on this thesis before. Bent views earlier AI products (Einstein, AgentForce) as weak and legacy siloed architecture as a long-term headwind.

#### Sell Triggers

- AgentForce adoption stalls
- revenue growth fails to sustain acceleration

> *"Nu ser det så ud til, at der er ved at komme en vending for Salesforce."*
